contract: Provider-neutral embedding interface: request (1..N bounded texts, optional provider-declared dimensions, input_type query | document | unspecified refused unsupported_feature where the provider lacks it, declared provider options, dispatch identity, deadline) admitted from a core/effect declaration with local refusals before any intent; the exact UTF-8 canonical JSON command payload admitted as EffectIntent arguments is bounded 1..65,536 bytes (too_large otherwise; not an HTTP-body limit); one provider call per dispatch through the delivery/effect-intent owner; outcomes completed{embeddings [%{index, vector}], descriptor{provider, model, dimensions, dtype float32, normalization unit_l2_verified | none}, usage, provenance} | refused{credentials_unavailable | invalid_request | unsupported_feature | too_large | authentication_failed | permission_denied | throttled | overloaded | not_found} | unknown{timeout | transport | malformed_response | provider_error}; exactly one vector per input with indices exactly 0..n-1 sorted by the validated index, each of the expected dimension, finite and within float32 range, and a served model equal to the requested one, otherwise unknown{malformed_response} with no vectors; unit_l2_verified only when every vector satisfies abs(norm_l2(v) - 1) <= 1.0e-3 (fixed, not configurable), otherwise normalization none; descriptors compatible only when all five fields are equal; throttled and overloaded failed/dispatched/retryable and not redispatched by default; only credentials_unavailable is attested no-send and retried; volatile result sink; provider behaviour and conformance kit.
limits: One call carries at most 65,536 bytes of canonical request JSON (the delivery/effect-intent argument bound): about 32 chunks of 2,000 ASCII graphemes or 8 of 2,000 four-byte graphemes; a caller groups inputs to fit and handles a refusal.

No automatic retry of a provider-reported throttle or overload: a caller retries only with its own ground, for example a new logical request reference accepting that the first request may have been processed.
The result sink is volatile local delivery: no durable retention, replay, recovery delivery or exactly-once delivery; after a restart only the settled status remains.
The completion seal is process-local integrity of the Adapter's own result, not provider authentication.
The descriptor's model is the requested model identifier, which the served model must equal; model aliases and snapshots need a later Contract.
Chunking, storage, similarity, int8 or binary dtypes, base64 encoding, batch-mode submission and caching are not supplied.
The failure table duplicates integration/ai-text's (same tags and delivery results) so the two interfaces stay independently copyable; a shared family outcome would be a new Piece.
Finite scenarios with a scripted test provider and a volatile store; no proof is claimed.

grounding.claim: Pinned Cure compilation type-checks the finite failure-tag to Contract-outcome and delivery-result decision; the static Binding table is checked equal to it at construction. Not a proof of provider behaviour.

Listed scenarios with a scripted test provider and the volatile Memory store: completed call path with vectors only through the sink; every conformance-kit scenario; local refusals before intent, credential and call; the canonical payload bound at exactly 65,536 and 65,537 bytes with escaping and whitespace; count, index-set, length, value and served-model defects unknown{malformed_response} with no vectors; reordering by validated index; the fixed norm tolerance on both sides; requested and native dimensions; retries (credentials_unavailable retried, throttled and overloaded unresolved and not redispatched, unknown never, also under redispatch_idempotent); second dispatch refused; classification table against Cure; envelope validation and seal; sink failures; descriptor compatibility; configuration and redaction; the batch-size example; a source audit of this Piece's own listed files. Finite scenarios, not proofs.
Relies on pinned compilation and nullary-sum erasure; not a local proof of the compiler.

Provider Pieces implement the behaviour truthfully: one HTTP exchange per call, failure tags chosen from documented statuses, items passed on as listed, absent usage fields reported :unknown; the host keeps the credential Need truthful; a provider's documented 'rejected before work' meaning of a throttle or overload is not relied on; one model identifier names one model whose vectors stay comparable.

telemetry.contract: No Elzoo event; provider libraries may emit their own events to consumer-installed handlers. Own events through runtime/telemetry: future task when a consumer needs them. Not inherited: runtime/telemetry is not a dependency.

config.contract: Construction-time binding (provider account entering the intent key), tenant, provider and its construction term, credential Need, model allowlist (each declared by the provider), inputs per call, bytes per input, canonical request bytes (at most 65,536), receive timeout and result sink; per-request deadline from the declaration; the norm tolerance is fixed by the Contract, not a setting; no hot reconfiguration.

control.contract: Call-scoped: dispatch, rearm and expiry are the delivery/effect-intent owner's Control; a deadline cannot erase a dispatched call, which is reported unknown.
